title: Village Sociographers and the 'Népi' Diagnosis
grammar: Counter-reality adversative clauses with holott ('whereas in fact')
goal: I can explain the aims and methods of the 1930s Hungarian village sociography (falukutatás) movement.
I can use holott to expose a contradiction between an official claim or appearance and the underlying reality.
I can discuss agrarian social history and literary sociography using B2 Hungarian vocabulary.

sections.title: Great Intellectual Debates: Urbanists vs. Populists
body: One of the best-known intellectual controversies of twentieth-century Hungarian culture was the debate between the 'népi' (populist / agrarian-sociographer) writers and the 'urbánus' (urbanist, city-oriented, liberal-minded) thinkers. Emerging in the interwar decades, both camps sought a cure for Hungary's semi-feudal inequalities, yet they looked into two very different mirrors of the nation.

In this unit, you will follow the village sociographers into the estates of the Alföld and Transdanubia, visit the editorial tables of the journal Szép Szó in Budapest, examine the arguments of István Bibó and Attila József, follow the 1985 meeting at Monor where members of the two camps talked openly with each other, and trace echoes of the debate after 1989. Grammatically, you will revisit the high-register polemical, adversative, and concessive connectors from B2 Unit 31 (holott, jóllehet, csakhogy, ellenben, ezzel szemben).
